description: Carbon is a nonmetallic chemical element with symbol C and atomic number 6. It is tetravalent, able to form up to four covalent bonds due to having 4 valence electrons, and belongs to group 14 of the periodic table. It is the 15th most abundant element in Earth's crust and the fourth most abundant in the universe by mass after hydrogen, helium, and oxygen.
uses: Carbon serves as the common element of all known life due to its abundance, unique diversity of organic compounds, and unusual ability to form polymers at temperatures commonly encountered on Earth. It is used in the iron and steel industry in smelting reactions and to control carbon content of steel. Carbon forms metallic carbides like tungsten carbide that are used as abrasives and for making hard tips for cutting tools, and graphene could potentially be used in space elevator construction and to store hydrogen for hydrogen-based engines.
characteristics: Carbon atoms can bond together in diverse ways resulting in various allotropes including graphite, diamond, amorphous carbon, and fullerenes. The physical properties vary widely: graphite is opaque, black, and soft enough to write with, while diamond is highly transparent and the hardest naturally occurring material. Graphite conducts electricity while diamond has low electrical conductivity, and under normal conditions diamond, carbon nanotubes, and graphene have the highest thermal conductivities of all known materials. Carbon has the highest sublimation point of all elements and is chemically resistant, resisting all but the strongest oxidizers at standard temperature and pressure.
